subtitle: Stone Prayers in a Shared Sacred Land

panels.shot: wide, slightly low-angle view over half-buried stone icons amid red earth mounds and brick stupa ruins at dusk
panels.action: The Pilak Artisan (Samatata–Pāla Era) stands in the foreground, chisel in hand, between a serene sandstone Buddha on one side and a fierce stone Shiva-Narasimha on the other, as ancient brick mounds rise behind him under a fading sky.

dialogue.text: In Pilak, long before the Manikyas, Buddha and Shiva shared the same red earth, and the stones remember what the chronicles forgot.

i18n.hi: माणिक्याओं से बहुत पहले, पिलक की लाल मिट्टी पर बुद्ध और शिव एक साथ थे – और पत्थर वो याद रखते हैं जो इतिहास भूल गया।

panels.shot: high aerial establishing shot sweeping over lush green rice fields, scattered mounds and low laterite ridges around Pilak
panels.action: An expansive rural landscape of South Tripura stretches to the horizon, with tiny brick mounds and half-buried stones dotting the fields near a small village path.

dialogue.text: Today Pilak seems a quiet corner of South Tripura, near Jolaibari, but beneath its fields lie centuries of brick, terracotta and stone from an older world called Samatata.

i18n.hi: आज पिलक दक्षिण त्रिपुरा में जोलाईबाड़ी के पास शांत सा दिखता है, पर खेतों के नीचे समतट नाम की पुरानी दुनिया की सदियों पुरानी ईंटें, मृण्मूर्ति और पत्थर दबे हैं।

panels.shot: medium close-up on a farmer’s foot nudging a carved stone half-buried in soil
panels.action: A weathered bare foot pushes aside loose soil to reveal the curved edge of a carved sandstone slab emerging from the earth.

dialogue.text: For generations, villagers turned up strange carved stones in their fields—faces, halos, lotus petals—without knowing they were fragments of an 8th to 12th century sacred landscape.

i18n.hi: पीढ़ियों तक गाँववालों को खेतों से अजीब नक्काशीदार पत्थर मिले – चेहरे, प्रभामंडल, कमल की पंखुड़ियाँ – पर उन्हें नहीं पता था ये 8वीं–12वीं सदी के पवित्र जगत के टुकड़े हैं।

panels.shot: time-shift transition, slow push-in from the unearthed stone to the same stone being carved centuries earlier
panels.action: The scene morphs into the past: The Pilak Artisan kneels by a sandstone block, carving a calm Buddha face as chips scatter around his feet in a forested workshop.

dialogue.text: We travel back to when Pilak’s stones were new, in the Samatata–Pāla horizon, when artisans shaped sandstone into Buddhas, goddesses and gods for patrons who crossed many paths of faith.

i18n.hi: हम लौटते हैं उस समय में जब पिलक के पत्थर नए थे – समतट–पाल काल में – जब कलाकार बलुआ पत्थर को बुद्ध, देवियों और देवों में ढालते थे, उन संरक्षकों के लिए जो अलग–अलग आस्थाओं के रास्तों से आते थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of an open-air workshop under trees filled with half-finished sculptures
panels.action: Under tall trees, The Pilak Artisan and fellow craftsmen work amid rows of unfinished images—an Avalokitesvara with many arms, a Surya with radiating halo, a fierce Narasimha—stacked beside brick moulds and terracotta plaques.

dialogue.text: Here the Pilak artisans answered many calls: from Buddhist monasteries, from Shaiva and Vaishnava shrines, from village cults of goddesses, all asking for form in stone and clay.

i18n.hi: यहाँ पिलक के कारीगरों ने कई पुकारों का जवाब दिया – बौद्ध विहारों से, शैव–वैष्णव मंदिरों से, गाँव की देवी–देवता परंपराओं से – सबने पत्थर और मिट्टी में रूप माँगा।

panels.shot: medium shot focusing on the artisan carving Avalokitesvara with delicate precision
panels.action: The Pilak Artisan leans close to a standing sandstone Avalokitesvara, carefully chiselling a tiny seated Buddha in the crown while assistants hold the figure steady.

dialogue.text: From Pilak came Avalokitesvara in sandstone, his crown holding a tiny Buddha, proof that Mahayana and Vajrayana currents of the Pāla world reached this eastern frontier.

i18n.hi: यहीं से पिलक ने बलुआ पत्थर का अवलोकितेश्वर दिया, जिसके मुकुट में छोटा बुद्ध बैठा है – सबूत कि पाल जगत की महायान–वज्रयान धाराएँ इस पूर्वी सीमा तक पहुँचीं।

panels.shot: three-quarter view of the artisan carving a goddess Chunda beside a proto-Marichi figure
panels.action: The Pilak Artisan chips at a multi-armed goddess figure, Chunda, while another sculptor beside him outlines a radiant female deity, Marichi, both resting against a backdrop of stacked stone blocks.

dialogue.text: Chunda and Marichi also grew under their tools—tantric goddesses of Buddhist tradition—sharing the same workshop where other hands prepared images for Hindu shrines.

i18n.hi: चुंडा और मारिची भी इन्हीं औज़ारों से उभरीं – बौद्ध तंत्र परंपरा की देवियाँ – उसी कार्यशाला में जहाँ दूसरी हथेलियाँ हिन्दू मंदिरों के लिए मूर्तियाँ गढ़ रही थीं।

panels.shot: wide, slightly low-angle shot of a brick stupa under construction near a shrine with a Hindu image
panels.action: Beyond the workshop, workers raise a tiered brick stupa while, just a short distance away, another group installs a stone image of Surya in a small Hindu shrine, both structures rising from the same mound.

dialogue.text: Brick stupas rose near shrines to Surya and Narasimha, so close that one could hear both the Buddhist chant and the priest’s mantra carried by the same wind.

i18n.hi: ईंटों के स्तूप सूर्य और नरसिंह के मंदिरों के पास उठे, इतने करीब कि एक ही हवा बौद्ध मंत्रोच्चार और पुजारी के मंत्र दोनों को साथ ले जाती थी।

panels.shot: medium close-up of the artisan setting a Surya image in a shrine niche
panels.action: The Pilak Artisan lifts a sandstone Surya, with tall boots and lotus pedestal, into a niche, as a Brahmin priest watches approvingly, hands folded.

dialogue.speaker: the_pilak_artisans
dialogue.text: Stone does not choose between Surya and Buddha. We only listen, and carve.

i18n.hi: पत्थर सूर्य और बुद्ध में भेद नहीं करता। हम बस सुनते हैं, और तराशते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on the artisan pressing a terracotta seal into wet clay
panels.action: The Pilak Artisan presses a small terracotta seal into a clay tablet, its circular design leaving a clear impression as rows of similar seals dry on a mat beside him.

dialogue.text: Terracotta seals and plaques carried stupas, lotus motifs and script, signs of monasteries and lay donors, linking Pilak to Samatata’s riverine networks and the Pāla realms beyond.

i18n.hi: टेराकोटा मुहरों और पट्टिकाओं पर स्तूप, कमल और लिपि उकेरी गई – विहारों और गृहस्थ दाताओं के निशान – जो पिलक को समतट की नदी–नालों और दूर के पाल राज्यों से जोड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Pilak’s sacred hill with multiple brick mounds, stupas and shrines in use
panels.action: From a hilltop, Pilak’s sacred zone appears alive: brick stupas, small temples with sculpted doorframes, smoke from offerings, monks and householders moving along the same paths.

dialogue.text: Archaeologists later named these mounds Sundari Tilla, Deb Bari and more, but in this age they were simply sacred hills, where Buddhists, Shaivas and Vaishnavas marked the same ground as holy.

i18n.hi: पुरातत्त्वविदों ने बाद में इन टीलों को सुंदरि टिल्ला, देव बाड़ी वगैरह नाम दिए, पर इस युग में ये बस पवित्र डोंगरियाँ थीं, जहाँ बौद्ध, शैव और वैष्णव एक ही धरती को पावन मानते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot, intimate, artisan conversing quietly with a Buddhist monk and a Hindu patron
panels.action: The Pilak Artisan stands between a robed monk and a Brahmin householder, each holding a palm-leaf manuscript, as they discuss over a newly finished stone figure resting on a wooden plank.

dialogue.text: Patrons came with different doctrines, but they turned to the same hands. The artisans learned to read not only scriptures, but faces—of monks, of priests, of local chiefs seeking merit and prestige.

i18n.hi: संरक्षक अलग–अलग मत लेकर आए, पर हाथ वही थे। कारीगरों ने सिर्फ शास्त्र ही नहीं, चेहरों को भी पढ़ना सीखा – भिक्षुओं के, पुजारियों के, और पुण्य–यश चाहने वाले स्थानीय सरदारों के।

panels.shot: time-lapse style shot where the workshop fades and jungle growth overtakes the structures
panels.action: The bustling workshop scene fades into stillness as the structures crumble; creepers, roots and trees slowly claim the stupas and shrines, while the Pilak Artisan’s figure becomes a ghostly outline before vanishing.

dialogue.text: Over time, the patrons changed, the monasteries thinned, kingdoms shifted, and the jungle walked back in. The stones stayed, half-buried, holding their intertwined stories in silence.

i18n.hi: समय के साथ संरक्षक बदले, विहार सूने हुए, राज्य खिसकते रहे और जंगल फिर लौट आया। पत्थर वहीं रहे, आधे दबे, अपनी गुँथी कहानियाँ चुपचाप सँभाले।

panels.shot: modern-era shot of ASI archaeologists brushing dust off a buried Buddha head
panels.action: In the 1960s, an archaeologist in khaki clothes crouches carefully, brushing soil from a sandstone Buddha head emerging from a trench, while a surveyor’s tripod stands nearby.

dialogue.text: In the late 20th century, the Archaeological Survey of India began to listen again, clearing mounds, mapping bricks, registering Pilak as a protected site in 1999.

i18n.hi: 20वीं सदी के अंत में भारतीय पुरातत्व सर्वेक्षण ने फिर सुनना शुरू किया – टीले साफ किए, ईंटें नापीं, और 1999 में पिलक को संरक्षित स्थल दर्ज किया।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Sundari Tilla area under excavation, showing brick stupa bases
panels.action: Excavators stand amid squared trenches at Sundari Tilla, exposing circular brick stupa bases and pathways, with tags marking structures under a bright sky.

dialogue.text: Near Sundari Tilla, fresh stupa bases appeared from the soil, confirming what B. Bhowmik and others read in the fragments—Pilak was part of a Buddhist and Hindu frontier between Samatata and the Pāla world.

i18n.hi: सुंदरि टिल्ला के पास मिट्टी से नए स्तूप–आधार निकले, जिससे बी. भौमिक और अन्य के पढ़े टुकड़े पक्के हुए – पिलक समतट और पाल जगत के बीच बौद्ध–हिन्दू सीमा प्रदेश का हिस्सा था।

panels.shot: interior shot of the Tripura Government Museum gallery displaying Pilak sculptures
panels.action: Inside the Ujjayanta Palace museum, visitors walk past carefully lit Pilak sculptures—Avalokitesvara, Surya, Narasimha and goddess figures—each mounted on pedestals with soft shadows.

dialogue.text: In 2013, the Tripura Government Museum at Ujjayanta arranged Pilak’s stones side by side—Buddhist, Shaiva, Vaishnava—so that modern eyes could see what the artisans once saw as a single field of work.

i18n.hi: 2013 में उज्जयंता के त्रिपुरा राज्य संग्रहालय ने पिलक के पत्थरों को साथ–साथ रखा – बौद्ध, शैव, वैष्णव – ताकि आज की आँखें देख सकें जो कारीगरों ने कभी एक ही कार्य–क्षेत्र की तरह देखा था।

panels.shot: medium shot of the Dalai Lama walking among Pilak ruins during his 2007 visit
panels.action: The Dalai Lama walks gently between low brick mounds and standing sculptures at Pilak, hands joined, as monks and officials follow quietly behind him.

dialogue.text: In 2007, the Dalai Lama’s visit drew global notice to this quiet site, reminding the world that Tripura once lay within wider Buddhist networks that touched Bengal, Assam and beyond.

i18n.hi: 2007 में दलाई लामा की यात्रा ने इस शांत स्थान पर दुनिया की नज़र लाई, याद दिलाया कि त्रिपुरा कभी उन बौद्ध जालों का हिस्सा था जो बंगाल, असम और आगे तक फैले थे।

panels.shot: wide transitional shot from Pilak ruins to a stylised Manikya-era palace skyline in the distance
panels.action: The camera rises over the Pilak mounds and then dissolves into the silhouette of a later Manikya-era palace and temple complex on the horizon, shimmering like a mirage beyond the ruins.

dialogue.text: When the Manikya kingdom later rose, it did not build Pilak, but it inherited the land, its memory and its mixed sacred forms, layered beneath new temples and courts.

i18n.hi: जब बाद में माणिक्य राज्य उठा, उसने पिलक को नहीं बनाया, पर इस भूमि, इसकी स्मृति और इसकी मिश्रित पवित्र छवियों को विरासत में लिया, जो नए मंदिरों और दरबारों के नीचे परतों में छिपी रहीं।

panels.shot: close-up on the Pilak Artisan’s imagined face superimposed over present-day ruins at sunset
panels.action: The faint, imagined face of The Pilak Artisan appears ghost-like over a present-day view of Pilak’s brick mounds and scattered sculptures at sunset, his eyes calm and distant.

dialogue.text: Pilak’s artisans left no chronicle and no royal titles, only stone where Buddha met Shiva; in their quiet craft we see how kingdoms grow from older roots they may never fully know.

i18n.hi: पिलक के कारीगर कोई इतिहास नहीं छोड़ गए, न राज–उपाधियाँ – बस वो पत्थर जहाँ बुद्ध मिले शिव से; उनकी शांत कारीगरी में दिखता है कि राज कितने पुराने, अनजाने जड़ों से उगते हैं।

title_i18n.hi: पिलक: जहाँ बुद्ध मिले शिव से

subtitle_i18n.en: Stone Prayers in a Shared Sacred Land
subtitle_i18n.hi: साझी पवित्र धरती पर पत्थर की प्रार्थनाएँ
